intent: Wrap one message of the transcript so the scroller can target it by id, track whether it is in view and anchor the view to it.
typical_uses: One message row of a transcript, identified by its `messageId`
The newest turn, marked with `scrollAnchor` so it is brought to the top of the view when it arrives

dont_use_when.situation: The layout of the message itself, its avatar, side, header and footer

invariants.text: The item renders `data-message-id` from `messageId` and `data-scroll-anchor` as `"true"` or `"false"` from `scrollAnchor`; only an item with a `messageId` can be reached by `scrollToMessage` or reported by useMessageScrollerVisibility.

When newly appended items include ones carrying `scrollAnchor`, the scroller aligns the first of them to the top of the viewport, leaving the provider's `scrollMargin` plus `scrollPreviousItemPeek` pixels of the content before it in view, and sizes the spacer so the position is reachable; this holds with `autoScroll` on too, except that more than one new anchored item arriving together while the scroller follows the end scrolls to the end instead. The scroller reacts to items being added or removed, not to `scrollAnchor` changing on an item already mounted.

anti_patterns.dont: Mark every item with `scrollAnchor` expecting the view to follow the end
anti_patterns.do_instead: Mark only the turns that should be brought to the top when they arrive, and call `scrollToEnd` from useMessageScroller where the end is the wanted position

good.title: An item holding a Message row

bad.title: An item without an id, expected to be reached by scrollToMessage
bad.why: `key` is React's and never reaches the item; without `messageId` the item is not registered, so `scrollToMessage(message.id)` cannot find it.
